title: Discrete structure
summary: A precise notion of discreteness depends on the ambient structure; in topology, a discrete space has every singleton open.

context.note: Framework is named textually in this seed release; full recursive first-principles closure remains future work.

assumptions.text: A set X with a topology is specified.

content.plain: A discrete description treats states as individually separable rather than forcing arbitrarily close intermediate states.
content.exact: A topological space X is discrete iff every subset of X is open; equivalently, every singleton {x} is open.
content.example: The integers with the discrete topology are a discrete topological space.
content.caveat: “Discrete = maximal information” is not a universal theorem. Information content depends on encoding, probability model, resolution, and task.

relations.note: Continuity is a property of maps between topological spaces, including discrete ones.
Sequences are naturally indexed by a discrete set such as N.
